---
address: norway.finance.bankCode
description: All 2306 bank identifiers (bankregisternummer) allocated in Norway — the first FOUR digits of every Norwegian account number, which is the country's equivalent of a sort code and needs no separate field because it is already inside the account. Norway allocates these by the thousand rather than one per bank: DNB alone holds 1 100 of them and Nordea 411, the sediment of two centuries of savings-bank mergers in which the acquirer kept the acquired bank's numbers so customers would not have to change their account. That is why a "bank code" here does not identify a bank one-to-one, and why 99 banks need 2 306 codes. Leading zeros are significant: 0500 is DNB. Source: Bits AS, Norwegian BIC Table.
